editorial:
The Gorilla (1939) is a 20th Century-Fox horror-comedy directed by Allan Dwan, with a running time of about 66 minutes. The Ritz Brothers, Bela Lugosi, Lionel Atwill, Anita Louise and Patsy Kelly are in the cast. It adapts Ralph Spence's 1925 stage play.

The rights question is the film's copyright status, which we could not settle. The renewal hit our script found is for Gorilla Hunt, a different Columbia short, so it should be ignored. Our scan of the 1966-1968 Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes was truncated and no Copyright Office search was completed, so the print stays undetermined. Check the 1966-1968 volumes by hand before relying on it commercially. The music credits and the play's rights history also remain unchecked.
faq: Is The Gorilla (1939) safe to reuse?

Not yet confirmed. The renewal hit our script found is for a different Columbia short, Gorilla Hunt. We could not complete a search of the Catalog of Copyright Entries or the Copyright Office records, so check them yourself first. Prints on the Internet Archive are uploads of unknown provenance.
Does the 1925 play affect the film?

It could. The film adapts Ralph Spence's 1925 play, and the play's copyright term and publication history need separate checking. We did not verify them. A film's status does not settle the status of its source material.
